{{Short description|Type of permutation}}
In mathematics, a '''vexillary permutation''' is a [[permutation]] ''μ'' of the positive integers containing no [[permutation pattern|subpermutation]] isomorphic to the permutation (2143); in other words, there do not exist four numbers ''i''&nbsp;<&nbsp;''j''&nbsp;<&nbsp;''k''&nbsp;<&nbsp;''l'' with ''μ''(''j'')&nbsp;<&nbsp;''μ''(''i'')&nbsp;<&nbsp;''μ''(''l'')&nbsp;<&nbsp;''μ''(''k''). They were introduced by {{harvs|txt|last1=Lascoux|last2=Schützenberger|year1=1982|year2=1985}}. The word "vexillary" means flag-like, and comes from the fact that vexillary permutations are related to [[flag (linear algebra)|flags]] of [[module (mathematics)|modules]].

{{harvtxt|Guibert|Pergola|Pinzani|2001}} showed that vexillary [[involution (mathematics)|involutions]] are enumerated by [[Motzkin number]]s.

==See also==
*[[Riffle shuffle permutation]], a subclass of the vexillary permutations
